sources.citation: Fargetti, Cristina Martins & Carmen L. Reis Rodrigues. 2008. Consoantes do Xipaya e do Juruna – uma comparação em busca do proto-sistema. Alfa (São Paulo) 52(2): 535-563.

sources.note: Nothing on Manitsawá stress. Manitsawá appears only as the extinct third member of the family: 'juntamente com o Manitsawá, já extinto (sobre o qual há apenas uma lista de palavras de STEINEN, 1942)' (p. 538) and 'Quanto ao povo manitsawá, nada se pode afirmar, não há relatos' (p. 540). The stress rule given on p. 545 ('Ocorre acento na primeira sílaba com tom alto da esquerda para a direita. Caso todos os tons sejam iguais, o acento recai sobre a última sílaba') is for Juruna/Yudja (yuru1259), not Manitsawá.

sources.citation: Schuller, Rodolpho R. 1911. Las lenguas indígenas de la Cuenca del Amazonas y del Orinoco. Revista Americana (Rio de Janeiro). Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú copy.

sources.note: No description of Manitsauá at all; only three Manitsauá words copied from von den Steinen inside long comparative lists (madigá 'luna', hayadí 'sol', itapa 'pescado'), reproducing Steinen's final-syllable accent marks. Wikipedia's 9-word 'Manitsauá vocabulary' is drawn from this.

sources.citation: von den Steinen, Karl. 1886. Durch Central-Brasilien: Expedition zur Erforschung des Schingú im Jahre 1884. Leipzig: F. A. Brockhaus. Anhang V, section "VI. Manitsauá", pp. 360-361 (vocabulary), pp. 211-212 and 323-324 (how and from whom the words were elicited).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The Manitsauá section gives only a vowel inventory (with nasalized ã ũ ĩ), a consonant table, one remark on medial clusters (tr, bl) and a 65-item wordlist; there is NO prose statement on Manitsauá accent. The wordlist itself carries an acute accent on nearly every item, almost always on the final syllable (humiá 'Haut', iyabiapá 'Haar', hayadí 'Sonne', madigaú 'Mond', hidagú 'Wasser', itapá 'Fisch', hayugú 'Hund', diadiá 'schwarz', anayú 'trinken'; exceptions: kele 'Steinbeil' unmarked, í-buá 'grün' double-marked).
